Create a hero split into two equal columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** is filled entirely by one large image that spans the full width and height of the column (the image covers the column area edge-to-edge with no internal padding).

**Right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small pill-shaped badge composed of a tiny leading icon and a short label on its own line; a left-aligned heading on its own line directly below the badge; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal row of two CTA buttons sitting side by side on the same baseline (a primary button on the left and a secondary button on the right), placed at the bottom of the column beneath the paragraph.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the image column first and the content column directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

prompts.title: Pricing Section
prompts.description: Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the ...
prompts.template:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the heading block, place a horizontal row of three pricing cards of equal width. The middle card is visually elevated (taller than the two side cards, sitting on a distinct filled background) and carries a small "Most popular" pill badge anchored to the center of its top edge. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a short single-line description directly below the name; a large dominant price with a small "/month" suffix on the same baseline to the right of the amount; one full-width primary call-to-action button (the middle card's button may use a contrasting treatment to reinforce its featured status); and a vertical list of feature rows (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline).

On narrow viewports the three cards stack vertically with the highlighted middle card preserving its position in the sequence; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

prompts.title: Feature Section 1
prompts.description: Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned header block composed of a large multi...
prompts.template:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned header block composed of a large multi-line heading on its own line followed by a short supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading (constrain the paragraph to a moderate reading width so it does not span the full container).

Below the header, place a three-column by two-row grid of six feature blocks with consistent gutters between columns and rows. Each block is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small rounded-square icon container at the top (the container holds a single glyph centered inside it); a medium-weight title on its own line directly below the icon container; a short multi-line description paragraph directly below the title, left-aligned and matching the block width.

On narrow viewports collapse the grid to two columns first, then to a single column on the narrowest breakpoints, preserving left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

prompts.title: Feature Section 2
prompts.description: Create a feature section framed as one large rounded outer container with comfortable outer margin on all sides so the entire section reads as a single card flo...
prompts.template:
Create a feature section framed as one large rounded outer container with comfortable outer margin on all sides so the entire section reads as a single card floating within the page.

Inside the container, use a three-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints.

The **left column** is wider than the other two and carries a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a text-style link on its own line below the paragraph whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text.

The **middle column** and the **right column** are narrower and equal in width; each stacks two feature blocks vertically with consistent spacing between them (four blocks total across both columns). Each feature block is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small rounded-square icon container (holding a single centered glyph); a short bold sub-heading on its own line directly below the icon; a supporting paragraph directly below the sub-heading that aligns flush-left with the icon and heading above it.

Allow a very subtle geometric grid texture to appear only behind part of the card interior (for example occupying one corner or a diagonal band) so it reads as a soft decorative surface without competing with the text content.

On narrow viewports, stack the three columns in reading order with the intro column first, the middle feature column second, and the right feature column third; keep all internal stacks in their original order.

prompts.title: CTA 1
prompts.description: Create a CTA section as one centered vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large multi-line primary...
prompts.template:
Create a CTA section as one centered vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large multi-line primary heading centered horizontally on its own line. Below the heading, place a supporting paragraph set at a restrained max width and centered horizontally so long lines do not stretch edge to edge.

Below the paragraph, center a single horizontal row containing two buttons sitting side by side with a small gap between them (approximately 16 px). The first button is a solid primary brand button with a short label; the second button is a secondary outlined button with a short label. Both buttons use pill-shaped or softly rounded corners and share the same height so they read as one balanced pair. The row itself is centered beneath the paragraph (one flex row, items centered, never wrapping to a second line on any viewport wider than the minimum supported width).

prompts.title: CTA 2
prompts.description: Create a CTA section as one vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned copy block containin...
prompts.template:
Create a CTA section as one vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned copy block containing, in order from top to bottom: a large heading on its own line; a first supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a second supporting paragraph directly beneath the first (the two paragraphs are separate elements, not one merged block); a short bold sub-heading on its own line that introduces the interactive card area below (for example a "see more" style label).

Below the copy block, leave clear vertical space, then place a two-column by two-row grid of horizontal resource cards on large 1280 px width breakpoints. Each card is laid out as a single horizontal row containing, from left to right: a small square brand mark (icon or logo glyph) flush to the left edge of the card; a middle vertical stack pairing a bold title line on top with a smaller description paragraph directly beneath it; a trailing rightward arrow affordance flush to the right edge of the card indicating navigation. One card may use a filled surface treatment (subtle background tint) so it reads as featured or hovered, while the remaining cards stay bordered with a light surface. Give every card thin outer borders, softly rounded corners, and consistent internal padding.

On narrow viewports, collapse the grid to a single column and stack the four cards in their original reading order (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).

prompts.title: Content 1
prompts.description: Create a content section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two column...
prompts.template:
Create a content section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two columns share the same vertical center line.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; then a horizontal row of two CTA buttons sitting side by side (a primary button whose label pairs with a small trailing arrow icon at the right end of the label, and a secondary button whose label pairs with a small leading eye icon at the left end of the label). Keep consistent vertical spacing between the heading, paragraph, and button row.

The **right column** contains one large rectangular media block sized to a 16 : 9 video-frame aspect ratio that fills the column width. Center a circular play-button control on top of the media block (the control sits at the exact horizontal and vertical center of the rectangle and carries a small triangular play glyph inside it). The media block may carry a placeholder background image or a solid filled surface behind the play control.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically with the text-and-buttons column first and the media block beneath it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

prompts.title: Content 2
prompts.description: Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.
prompts.template:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **header block** sits at the top and is horizontally centered: a large heading on its own line, then a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading constrained to a restrained max line width (roughly two-thirds of the content area) so it does not span the full container.

The **timeline band** sits below the header block. A thin horizontal baseline rule runs the full content width with small circular markers placed along it at even intervals. Anchor four milestone columns above or along the baseline, evenly spaced across the width. Each milestone is a vertical stack containing, in order: a small date badge at the top (the badge is a compact inline row pairing a small leading calendar icon with a short date string on the same baseline); a bold short title on its own line directly beneath the badge; a placeholder description paragraph of two to three lines beneath the title; and a text-style link whose label includes a small trailing arrow icon anchored at the bottom of the milestone stack. Maintain equal horizontal gutters between milestone columns.

On narrow viewports, reflow the timeline into a single-column vertical stack while preserving chronological top-to-bottom order; each milestone keeps its internal stacking sequence intact.

prompts.title: Contact 1
prompts.description: Create a contact section as a single centered vertical stack on a 640px width page background, constrained to a comfortable reading max width and centered horiz...
prompts.template:
Create a contact section as a single centered vertical stack on a 640px width page background, constrained to a comfortable reading max width and centered horizontally with generous side padding.

At the very top, place a main page heading on its own line, centered horizontally. Directly below the heading, place a short supporting paragraph (one to two lines) that references technical issues, product feedback, and business-plan questions, also centered.

Below the supporting paragraph, stack a vertical form whose fields read top to bottom in this order: a labeled email input row (the label sits above the input on its own line and pairs a short label text with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting a company email address); a labeled subject input row in the same shape directly below (the label sits above with a required-field marker; the input carries a leading pen or tag icon affordance and a placeholder inviting a short subject line); a labeled multi-line message textarea directly below that (the label sits above with a required-field marker and an optional small circular question-mark information affordance to the right of the label; the textarea carries a placeholder inviting the user to write their message and allows vertical expansion).

Finish the section with a horizontal flex row of two actions placed beneath the form, separated by a small inline gap: a secondary control at the left whose label combines a leading back-arrow glyph and short text that navigates back to the homepage; a primary control at the right whose label combines short send text and a trailing send-arrow glyph. Both controls sit on the same baseline and stretch to equal widths within the row.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column stack, let the form occupy full content width with comfortable side padding, and stack the two action controls vertically (secondary above primary) if horizontal space is insufficient.

prompts.title: Contact 2
prompts.description: Create a contact section that reads as a single centered vertical stack constrained to a 1280px width container with comfortable side padding.
prompts.template:
Create a contact section that reads as a single centered vertical stack constrained to a 1280px width container with comfortable side padding.

At the top, place a large multi-line heading (sentence case or title case) on its own line, left-aligned within the container. Directly below the heading, place one short supporting line about guidance, support, and tailored solutions on its own line.

Below the supporting line, span a single full-width horizontal media band (photograph or illustration) that stretches across the entire content width, with a moderate aspect ratio so it reads as a cinematic strip.

Under the media band, stack three horizontal directory bands separated by generous vertical rhythm (each band separated from the next by whitespace or a subtle horizontal rule).

**First band** begins with a small section label prefixed by a decorative turn or bullet-like marker, left-aligned on its own line. Below the label, the band splits into two equal columns on large 1280px width breakpoints: the left column carries a short category label (general hello) on its own line followed by a single email address on the next line; the right column carries a short category label (enquiries) on its own line followed by a different email address on the next line.

**Second band** follows the same structure: a small prefixed section label on its own line, then two columns below. The left column carries a postal-address label on its own line and a full multi-line street address beneath it; the right column carries a map-related label on its own line and a text link to get directions beneath it.

**Third band** follows the same structure: a small prefixed section label on its own line, then two columns below. The left column carries a social-platforms label on its own line and a vertical list of platform names rendered as text links beneath it; the right column carries a phone label on its own line and one or more listed telephone numbers beneath it.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns within each band vertically (left column first, right column second) while keeping the section labels and media band at full width.

prompts.title: Logo Section 1
prompts.description: Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding. At the very top, place a short cente...
prompts.template: Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding. At the very top, place a short centered kicker line on its own row naming the social-proof intent (for example a sentence stating that the product is trusted by teams worldwide). Below the kicker, leave a small vertical gap, then center a single horizontal flex row of exactly six partner marks or logotypes that share one visual weight; space the marks with even horizontal gaps so they read as one unified band. No secondary heading is required unless you add a very small optional sub-line directly beneath the kicker on its own centered row. On narrow viewports the mark row wraps into additional centered rows while keeping even horizontal spacing between items and consistent vertical gaps between wrapped lines.

prompts.title: Logo Section 2
prompts.description: Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding.
prompts.template:
Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding.

The **header block** sits at the top of the stack, centered horizontally, and contains in order from top to bottom: a primary heading on its own line; one supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading, held at a restrained max width so the line length stays comfortable; and below the paragraph a single horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side with a small gap between them (each link label includes a trailing arrow character at the end of the wording).

Leave clear vertical space beneath the header block, then present six partner marks, each placed inside its own card with the mark centered both horizontally and vertically within the card. Arrange the six cards in two centered rows of three cards each: the first row holds three cards, the second row holds three cards directly below, with equal horizontal gaps between cards and equal vertical gaps between the two rows.

On narrow viewports reflow the cards into fewer columns (for example two columns or a single column) while keeping the header block centered above and allowing the link row to wrap onto a second line if space is tight.

prompts.title: Team 1
prompts.description: Create a team section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a header row split into two halves on the same baseline:...
prompts.template:
Create a team section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a header row split into two halves on the same baseline: a left-aligned vertical stack containing a large heading on its own line and a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; and a single compact outlined button anchored to the right end of the row whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place one large transparent container with no shadow or borders. Inside the container, build a four-column by two-row grid of eight team member blocks with consistent gutters between columns and rows. Each block is a centered vertical stack containing, in order: a medium circular avatar image at the top; a small pill-shaped badge on its own line directly below the avatar (composed of a tiny leading icon and a short role-category label); the team member's name on its own line directly below the badge in medium weight; a single-line job title directly below the name in lighter weight; and a compact outlined button at the bottom of the block whose label is composed of a small leading icon and a short action label (e.g. "Contact me") on the same baseline.

On smaller breakpoints reduce the column count stepwise (four columns, then two, then one) until the blocks form a single column on the narrowest viewports; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

prompts.title: Social Proof 1
prompts.description: Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place a single horizontal row of three stat blocks centered on the...
prompts.template:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place a single horizontal row of three stat blocks centered on the page on the same baseline with generous spacing between them. Each stat block is a centered vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value (e.g. "73M+") on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Keep all text within each block horizontally centered.

On narrow viewports collapse the three stat blocks into a single column, stacking them vertically in left-to-right reading order with consistent spacing between them.

prompts.title: Social Proof 2
prompts.description: Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place one large rounded outer container with a thin outer boundary...
prompts.template:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place one large rounded outer container with a thin outer boundary that frames the entire section content so it reads as a single card.

Inside the container, place a horizontal row of four equal-width stat tiles on the same baseline with consistent gutters between them. Each tile is its own rounded rectangular panel containing a centered vertical stack composed of, in order: a small icon centered at the top; one large prominent numeric value on its own line directly below the icon; a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Keep all content within each tile horizontally centered.

Below the stat tiles, after comfortable vertical space, place a left-aligned trust row composed of a short introductory label (e.g. "Trusted by:") followed by a horizontal row of brand logos, each rendered as a small monochrome glyph with consistent spacing between them, all sitting on the same baseline as the label.

On narrow viewports collapse the four tiles into a two-column grid first, then into a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; the trust row wraps naturally beneath the label.

prompts.title: FAQ
prompts.description: Create a FAQ section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line.
prompts.template:
Create a FAQ section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line.

Below the heading, place a vertical stack of 6-8 accordion items with consistent spacing between them, constrained to a moderate max width and centered horizontally within the container. Each item is a self-contained collapsible row: in its collapsed state, the row is a horizontal composition of a small question-mark icon anchored to the left, a bold question label to the right of the icon on the same baseline, and a small chevron icon anchored to the far right of the row pointing downward. When expanded, the chevron rotates upward and a content region appears directly below the question row, containing one or more paragraphs of answer text at a comfortable reading width; inline text links may appear within the answer copy. Only one item should be expandable at a time (opening one collapses any previously open item).

On narrow viewports keep the single-column accordion stack centered; preserve reading order and ensure question rows and their answer regions remain full-width within the container.

prompts.title: Testimonial 1
prompts.description: Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place a single centered vertical stack composed of, in order: a la...
prompts.template:
Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place a single centered vertical stack composed of, in order: a large decorative opening quotation mark glyph centered on its own line at the top; a centered multi-line quote paragraph directly below the quotation mark at a moderate reading width; and a centered author attribution row on its own line directly below the quote. The author row is a horizontal composition of a small circular avatar thumbnail on the left, the author name immediately to the right of the avatar on the same baseline, a short separator character, and a role or company label to the right of the separator on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack; allow the quote paragraph to span the full content width with comfortable side padding.

prompts.title: Testimonial 2
prompts.description: Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a small pill...
prompts.template:
Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a small pill-shaped badge (containing a tiny leading icon and a short category label, both inside a rounded container) centered on its own line; a large centered heading on its own line directly below the badge; a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a moderate reading width; and a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, centered as a pair beneath the paragraph — each link label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place a horizontal carousel region spanning the full container width. The carousel displays three testimonial cards side by side in the visible frame with consistent gutters between them. Each card is a rounded rectangular panel containing a left-aligned vertical stack composed of, in order: a horizontal row of five small star icons on the same baseline at the top of the card; a bold testimonial title on its own line directly below the star row; a multi-line quote paragraph directly below the title; and an author attribution row at the bottom of the card composed of a small circular avatar thumbnail on the left, with a bold author name on its own line to the right of the avatar and a role or company label on a second line directly beneath the name, aligned with the name text. Position a circular previous-arrow navigation control on the left edge of the carousel and a circular next-arrow navigation control on the right edge, both vertically centered relative to the testimonial cards.

On narrow viewports the carousel shows one card at a time, the navigation controls remain anchored to the left and right edges, and the header links stack vertically if needed.

prompts.title: Blog 1
prompts.description: Create a blog section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned header row with a large heading on the le...
prompts.template:
Create a blog section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned header row with a large heading on the left (e.g. "Trending topics") and a text-style link anchored to the right of the same baseline whose label includes a small leading icon and the text "See all topics".

Below the header, place three equal-width columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a rounded panel with a thin outer boundary. Inside each panel, stack from top to bottom: a header row composed of a small icon on the left, a bold category name to the right of the icon on the same baseline, and a compact pill-shaped "View all" link anchored to the right of that same row whose label includes a trailing arrow; below the header row, a vertical list of five to six article link rows with consistent vertical spacing. Each link row is a horizontal composition of a small circular placeholder avatar on the left, a short article title rendered as a clickable link to the right of the avatar filling the available width, and a small trailing arrow icon anchored to the far right of the row — all elements on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports stack the three columns vertically in their original left-to-right reading order; each panel stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

prompts.title: Blog 2
prompts.description: Create a blog section as one centered vertical stack inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on i...
prompts.template:
Create a blog section as one centered vertical stack inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line (e.g. "Our Blog").

Below the heading, place a vertical stack of article entries separated by generous vertical space (no visible dividers between entries). Each entry is a centered vertical stack containing, in order: a small pill-shaped category badge composed of a tiny leading icon and a short category label, both centered horizontally on its own line; a large centered multi-line headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line directly below the badge; a centered author row on the same baseline composed of a small circular avatar on the left, the author name immediately to the right of the avatar, a small date icon and publication date label to the right of the name, a small views or shares icon and a numeric count to the right of the date — all elements sitting on a single horizontal line with subtle separators between them.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack with all entries in their original reading order; allow the author row elements to wrap naturally while preserving logical grouping.

prompts.title: Portfolio
prompts.description: Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below ...
prompts.template:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header block, place a three-column by two-row grid of six equal-width cards with consistent gutters between columns and rows. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a brand logo or mark centered on its own line; a project title centered on its own line directly below the logo; a short centered description paragraph directly below the title; and a text-style link at the bottom of the card composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon inside a compact outlined container.

On narrow viewports, collapse the grid stepwise from three columns to two, then to a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

prompts.title: Newsletter
prompts.description: Create a newsletter section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Position four large circular portrait photographs as decorative anch...
prompts.template:
Create a newsletter section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Position four large circular portrait photographs as decorative anchors around the perimeter of the section — one near the top-left, one near the top-right, one near the bottom-left, and one near the bottom-right — so they frame the central content without overlapping it.

In the center of the section, place a vertical stack containing, in order: a large centered heading on its own line; a centered supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal row on the same baseline composed of a full-width email text input on the left and a primary subscribe button on the right (the button label includes a trailing arrow icon), centered as a pair beneath the paragraph and constrained to a moderate width. Directly below the subscribe row, place a centered social-proof line composed of a tight horizontal cluster of slightly overlapping small circular user avatars on the left, a small "+" separator, and a short caption stating a subscriber count — all sitting on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack; let the email input and subscribe button wrap into a vertical pair if needed; keep the social-proof row centered below.

prompts.title: Event Schedule
prompts.description: Create an event schedule section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line; direc...
prompts.template:
Create an event schedule section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered text link whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text, on its own line.

Below the header, place a vertical list of session rows separated by thin horizontal rules spanning the full container width (one rule sits above the first row and one sits below the last row, creating a ruled band). Each session row is a single horizontal band composed of two inline elements on the same baseline: a time-range label left-aligned within a fixed-width leading column (e.g. "08:00 - 09:00"), and a session title to the right of the time column on the same baseline — every session title must be a link. Keep the time column width consistent across all rows so the session titles align vertically.

On narrow viewports, keep the same two-column row structure; if the container becomes too narrow for side-by-side alignment, stack the time label above the session title within each row, preserving the thin horizontal rules between rows.

prompts.title: Footer 1
prompts.description: Create a footer section as one centered vertical stack inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. Stack from top to bottom: a brand mark compos...
prompts.template:
Create a footer section as one centered vertical stack inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. Stack from top to bottom: a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline, centered horizontally on its own line; a single centered tagline paragraph directly below the brand mark at a moderate reading width; a horizontal row of navigation links sitting side by side on the same baseline, centered as a group directly below the tagline (each link is a short text label with consistent spacing between adjacent links); and a single centered copyright line on its own line at the bottom of the section, separated from the navigation row by comfortable vertical space.

On narrow viewports keep the entire stack centered; allow the navigation links to wrap into multiple lines if needed while preserving reading order.

prompts.title: Footer 2
prompts.description: Create a footer section as a single horizontal bar inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. On the left side of the bar, place one copyright ...
prompts.template:
Create a footer section as a single horizontal bar inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. On the left side of the bar, place one copyright line on its own baseline. On the right side of the same bar, place a horizontal row of small social-media icon links sitting side by side on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them.

On narrow viewports stack the copyright line above the social icon row, both centered, preserving reading order.

prompts.title: Cometitive Analysis
prompts.description: Competitive Analysis Report
prompts.template:
Competitive Analysis Report
Author: Your Name Here

Generate with AI
01
Company Background
Provide a comprehensive understanding of each competitor's foundational aspects. Include relevant history, operational scale, and financial stability to set the context.

Company Overview
Summarize the competitor’s history, company size, and present financial conditiion. Mention mission statements, vision, core values, and any unique attributes that set them apart.

Product/Service Overview
Detail the primary products or services offered by the competitor. Discuss key features, unique selling points, and target demographics, along with any notable variations in their offerings.

Leadership and Organizational Structure
Describe the key stakeholders and leadership team. Include organizational hierarchy, notable leadership changes, and their impact on strategy.

Financial Health
Provide an overview of the financial standing including revenue, profit margins, market share, and growth trajectory. Highlight significant financial milestones and stability signals.

Recent Developments and Future Plans
Identify any recent initiatives, strategic pivots, mergers, acquisitions, or future plans disclosed that indicate the direction they are heading towards.

02
Competitor Analysis
Conduct an in-depth analysis of each competitor's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. Compare this with your own product and market position.

SWOT Analysis
Perform a comprehensive SWOT analysis, detailing the internal strengths and weaknesses, as well as external opportunities and threats. Discuss specific examples and implications.

Product Comparison
Compare key product features, value propositions, and performance metrics against your offerings. Highlight competitive advantages and areas for improvement.

Customer Reviews and Feedback
Analyze customer reviews and feedback concerning the competitor’s product. Identify recurring positive and negative points and their impact on customer satisfaction.

Innovation and Technology
Assess the level of innovation and technology advancements employed by the competitor. Discuss R&D investments, tech partnerships, and their impact on the product.

Market Share and Growth
Evaluate the competitor's market share, growth trends, and strategic moves that have contributed to their current position. Consider geographical presence and market segments.

03
Market Positioning
Evaluate how competitors position themselves in the market, including brand perception, marketing strategies, and pricing tactics. Understanding these aspects will help identify gaps and opportunities for your product.

Market Perception
Explore how the market perceives the competitor brand. Discuss customer trust, brand reputation, and overall satisfaction levels.

Marketing and Pricing Strategy
Detail the competitor’s marketing approach, including digital, traditional, and social media. Describe their pricing strategies and positioning within the market in terms of value and affordability.

Customer Acquisition and Retention
Analyze the strategies competitors use to acquire new customers and retain existing ones. Discuss loyalty programs, membership benefits, and customer service quality.

Geographic and Demographic Targeting
Identify the primary geographic and demographic segments targeted by the competitor. Discuss regional strengths, local marketing initiatives, and niche demographics.

Brand Partnerships and Sponsorships
Detail any strategic partnerships, sponsorships, or endorsements that bolster the competitor's market position. Examine the effectiveness and impact of these alliances.

prompts.title: Feature Request
prompts.description:
Feature Request Document
Example
Feature Overview
Feature Name: Grammar Suggestion Tool

Feature Description: The Grammar Suggestion Tool aims to upscale SpeedScribble’s functionality by embedding advanced grammar correction capabilities. Its core purpose is to identify grammatical errors and recommend accurate corrections in real time, making the writing process efficient and error-free for users. It consists of a multi-language support system and real-time processing algorithms that integrate seamlessly with the existing text editor. This upgrade responds to the user demand for an intuitive tool that assists in producing grammatically sound content with minimal effort.

Business Justification
Business Alignment: The Grammar Suggestion Tool strongly aligns with SpeedScribble’s strategic goal of enhancing user experience. Elevating the quality of writing will drive higher user satisfaction and potentially increase user retention rates. This feature supports the company's KPIs, specifically those relating to user engagement and platform usage.

ROI Estimation: The development cost for the Grammar Suggestion Tool is projected at $200,000. Expected returns include a 15% increase in premium subscriptions due to enhanced functionality. The tool could also reduce customer churn by 10%, as satisfied users are less likely to switch to competitors. Cumulatively, a net revenue increase of approximately $500,000 annually is anticipated, driven by user retention and new subscriptions.

User Impact
Affected User Segments: This tool will primarily benefit professional writers, students, and non-native English speakers. Professional writers will enjoy seamless content creation with fewer errors, students will benefit from improved academic writing, and non-native speakers will gain confidence in their writing accuracy.

User Benefits: Key benefits include enhanced writing quality, decreased editing time, and real-time grammatical feedback. Users will experience increased confidence in their writing abilities, resulting in higher engagement and satisfaction levels. The tool is also expected to serve as an educational aid, helping users learn and avoid common grammatical mistakes.

Technical Considerations
Implementation Complexity: The integration of the Grammar Suggestion Tool is technically challenging due to the need for precise and sophisticated language processing algorithms. It requires robust multi-language support and seamless integration within the existing architecture of SpeedScribble.

Dependencies & Resources: Successful implementation will depend on collaboration with Natural Language Processing (NLP) experts and may require third-party API integration for advanced grammar checking capabilities. Key resources include a dedicated team of developers, language experts, and a budget for third-party services.

Risks & Mitigation: Potential risks involve the complexity of multi-language support and the varying rules of grammar across languages. To mitigate these risks, a phased rollout starting with English and gradually incorporating other languages is advised. Additionally, thorough testing and feedback loops with a small user base can preemptively address usability issues before broader deployment.

prompts.title: MPV Feature List
prompts.description:
Feature Overview
1. User Authentication
Feature Name: User Authentication

Feature Description: A biometrically-enabled secure gateway allowing users to confidently log into the app. This feature is paramount to enhancing appropriate data handling, ensuring user privacy, and building overall trust between the user and the application.

User Story: As a new user concerned about app security, I want to log in using biometric authentication so that I feel confident my data is protected, and I can access the app swiftly and securely.

Acceptance Criteria:

The system must recognize and validate fingerprints and facial recognition.
Must integrate with major biometric APIs on iOS and Android.
Should have backup authentication using PIN in case biometric fails.
Successful and unsuccessful login attempts must be logged appropriately.
Priority: High

Dependencies:

Integration with biometric authentication APIs.
Support for fallback PIN authentication.
User data encryption modules.
Risks and Mitigations:

Risk: Biometric failures might prevent access. Mitigation: Implement reliable backup PIN authentication.
Risk: API updates might affect functionality. Mitigation: Regularly monitor and update APIs.
2. Device Integration
Feature Name: Device Integration

Feature Description: A seamless integration element that connects the app with a range of third-party smart home devices. This feature enriches the user experience by providing centralized control over all smart home elements through a single application.

User Story: As a user with multiple smart home devices, I want to control all of them through a single app so that I have a streamlined and efficient smart home experience.

Acceptance Criteria:

Must support integration with major smart home device brands (e.g., Nest, Philips Hue, Samsung SmartThings).
Should allow adding, removing, and managing various smart devices through the app.
Must support real-time status monitoring of connected devices.
Priority: High

Dependencies:

Partnerships with smart home device manufacturers.
APIs and SDKs for third-party device integration.
Real-time data handling capabilities.
Risks and Mitigations:

Risk: Device compatibility issues. Mitigation: Extensive testing with major device brands.
Risk: Delays in API updates. Mitigation: Maintain close relationship with device manufacturers for timely updates.
3. Interface Personalization
Feature Name: Interface Personalization

Feature Description: Customizable interface options that allow users to personalize their app experience according to their preferences, enhancing the overall usability and satisfaction.

User Story: As a user who values personalized experiences, I want to customize the app’s interface so that it aligns with my personal preferences and improves my user experience.

Acceptance Criteria:

Must allow users to change app themes (light/dark mode).
Should support customizable dashboard layouts.
Must provide options to localize the app in multiple languages.
Priority: Medium

Dependencies:

Development of customizable UI components.
Multi-language support and localization services.
User preference data management.
Risks and Mitigations:

Risk: Complexity in managing multiple themes. Mitigation: Implement a robust theming architecture.
Risk: Localization inaccuracies. Mitigation: Use professional language translation services.
4. Social Sharing
Feature Name: Social Sharing

Feature Description: An engaging feature that allows users to share their smart home setups and experiences on various social media platforms, fostering a sense of community and encouraging app promotion.

User Story: As a satisfied user, I want to share my smart home setup on social media so that I can recommend the app to friends and showcase my smart home innovations.

Acceptance Criteria:

Integration with major social media platforms (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram).
Must allow sharing of screenshots and app-generated content.
Should include tracking of shared content for analytics purposes.
Priority: Low

Dependencies:

APIs for social media platform integration.
Development of content-sharing features.
User data tracking and analytics.
Risks and Mitigations:

Risk: Privacy concerns with shared content. Mitigation: Implement clear user consent protocols.
Risk: Changes in social media APIs. Mitigation: Regularly update integration points.
Priority Level
High Priority
User Authentication: Given the premium on online security and user trust, this feature is non-negotiable in the MVP. It directly impacts user retention and confidence which are crucial for the app's success.

Device Integration: As a core feature, this is essential to delivering on the promise of a comprehensive smart home controlling platform. It directly correlates with the app’s unique value proposition and must be included in the MVP.

Medium Priority
Interface Personalization: While notable in enhancing the user experience, this feature is not crucial for the initial launch. It can be developed in subsequent iterations after essential features have been established and fine-tuned.

Low Priority
Social Sharing: As an enriching component of user engagement, social sharing can be deferred until the app has a firm footing in its user base. While it offers value, it’s not critical for the MVP.

RoI Analysis:
User Authentication: High RoI as it lays the foundation of user trust and satisfaction, significant for long-term user retention and growth.

Device Integration: High RoI due to its direct correlation with the app’s core utility and unique value proposition. This feature is a primary driver for user acquisition and engagement.

Interface Personalization: Medium RoI since personalized experiences significantly boost user satisfaction and reduce churn rates in later stages.

Social Sharing: Low to Medium RoI focusing on user engagement and organic user acquisition through word-of-mouth, it becomes more valuable as user base grows.

Dependencies
Understanding dependencies is vital for efficient project management. Addressing them ensures that feature development proceeds smoothly without unforeseen interruptions.

User Authentication:

Integration with biometric authentication APIs.
Support for fallback PIN authentication.
User data encryption modules.
Device Integration:

Partnerships with smart home device manufacturers.
APIs and SDKs for third-party device integration.
Real-time data handling capabilities.
Interface Personalization:

Development of customizable UI components.
Multi-language support and localization services.
User preference data management.
Social Sharing:

APIs for social media platform integration.
Development of content-sharing features.
User data tracking and analytics.
prompts.template:
MVP Feature List
Author: Your Name Here

Generate with AI
01
Feature Overview
This section provides a detailed overview of each key feature included in the MVP. The objective is to define every feature's purpose and value clearly and succinctly. This clarity ensures stakeholders understand the function and benefits of each feature. It's imperative for setting the foundation of the product's direction and helping the team focus on essential features.

Feature Name
Assign an intuitive and descriptive name to each feature. The name should clearly convey the primary function or benefit and be easily understood by all stakeholders, including developers, designers, and end-users. Aim for simplicity and clarity. Avoid ambiguous or overly technical terms that may cause confusion.

Feature Description
Provide a concise yet comprehensive explanation of what the feature does. Highlight its core functionality and describe how it will enhance the user's experience. Include the problem it solves, its key benefits, and any innovative aspects. This section should make it clear why the feature is essential for the MVP.

User Story
Include a user story to provide real-world context. This should outline who the user is, what they want to achieve with the feature, and why it is important to them. User stories help to keep features user-centric and ground the development process in real-world use cases. Ensure the story addresses the user's needs and pain points.

Acceptance Criteria
Specify the acceptance criteria for each feature. These are the conditions that must be met for the feature to be considered complete. Clear acceptance criteria ensure that the feature meets the intended requirements and functions correctly. Acceptance criteria should be measurable and testable, encompassing both functional and non-functional aspects.

Priority
Classify the feature's priority to determine its inclusion in the MVP. Use categories like High, Medium, or Low to indicate its criticality and how it fits into the overall product strategy. Clearly defined priorities guide resource allocation and help the team stay focused on delivering the most impactful features first.

Dependencies
List any dependencies that must be resolved for the feature to be developed and implemented. This includes dependencies on other features, resources, or external systems. Identifying dependencies early helps in planning and avoiding bottlenecks, ensuring a smoother development process.

Risks and Mitigations
Identify any potential risks associated with the feature and outline mitigation strategies. This can include technical challenges, resource constraints, or market uncertainties. Being proactive about risk management helps ensure successful feature delivery.

02
Priority Level
This section aids in the precise determination of each feature's relative importance, guiding resource allocation and decision-making. Categorizing features by priority ensures that the MVP delivers maximum value with available resources. Prioritization is essential for focusing efforts on the most impactful features, maintaining a balance between immediate needs and long-term goals.

High Priority
Identify essential features that are crucial for the MVP's success. These features are non-negotiable and must be included to fulfill the primary value proposition of the product. They address critical user needs and deliver significant value. High-priority features should be the primary focus of the development team early on.

Medium Priority
Highlight features that add substantial value but are not critical for the initial launch. While beneficial, these features can be slated for later iterations if necessary. Prioritize based on available resources and time constraints. Medium priority features should be well-documented to ensure they can be seamlessly integrated in future updates.

Low Priority
List features that enhance the user experience but are not required for the MVP. These low-priority features can be postponed to future releases, ensuring the focus remains on delivering core value within the MVP timeline. Low-priority features should not distract from the critical path but can be considered for enhancing future versions of the product.

RoI Analysis
Conduct a thorough Return on Investment (RoI) analysis for each feature. Understanding the expected benefits versus development costs helps in making informed prioritization decisions. This assessment aids in optimizing resource allocation for maximum impact. Make sure to consider both short-term gains and long-term strategic value in your analysis.

Dependencies
Identify any dependencies that influence the prioritization of features. Dependencies may include other features, team availability, or external factors that impact development timelines and resource requirements. Clear understanding of dependencies helps in realistic planning and execution.

Stakeholder Input
Gather and incorporate input from all relevant stakeholders. Their perspectives can provide valuable insights into the prioritization process, ensuring that the most impactful features are addressed first. Regularly update and communicate the priority list to stakeholders to maintain alignment and transparency.

prompts.title: Product Requirement
prompts.description:
PRD (Product Requirement Document)
Example
SoundBubble PRD
Background
Problem Statement
In today's digital age, emerging artists struggle to find platforms where they can seamlessly share their music and grow their fanbase without getting lost in the noise of mainstream content. Many talented individuals don't have the resources or opportunities to promote their music effectively. As a result, they end up earning insufficient revenue to sustain their craft while music lovers miss out on discovering fresh talent.

Market Opportunity
The music streaming industry is poised to grow massively, with projections estimating it to exceed $76.91 billion by 2027. However, there's a clear gap in the market for platforms dedicated to unsigned and emerging talents. Mainstream platforms often overshadow these artists, and there's a significant demand among listeners to discover new music. Competitors like Spotify and Apple Music focus primarily on established artists, leaving a niche yet potentially lucrative market segment untapped.

User Personas
Aspiring Artists
Characteristics: Individuals aged 18-35, tech-savvy, passionate about music creation, and seeking platforms for exposure.
Needs: User-friendly interfaces to upload music, tools to promote their tracks, and opportunities for monetization.
Challenges: Limited promotional budgets, lack of visibility, and insufficient revenue streams.
Avid Music Fans
Characteristics: Individuals aged 15-40, diverse musical tastes, constantly on the hunt for new genres and artists.
Needs: Easy discovery of new music, curated playlists, and social features to share and discuss music.
Challenges: Overwhelmed by mainstream content, difficulty in finding unique, new music.
Vision Statement
SoundBubble aims to democratize music distribution by creating an inclusive platform where emerging artists can showcase their talent, connect with fans, and generate sustainable income. By harnessing the power of community-driven discovery and advanced technology, SoundBubble will redefine the landscape of music streaming, making it a haven for both artists and fans.

Product Origin
The idea for SoundBubble emerged from a recognition of the challenges faced by new artists in gaining visibility and achieving financial success. Initial brainstorming sessions with artists and music industry experts highlighted the urgent need for a dedicated platform. Early pilot studies were conducted where a small group of artists uploaded their tracks and engaged with users, providing invaluable feedback that shaped the concept into a scalable product idea.

Objectives
SMART Goals
Specific: Achieve a 25% increase in user base by Q1 through targeted marketing campaigns and platform enhancements.
Measurable: Track user growth, artist sign-ups, and revenue increments via analytics dashboards.
Achievable: Leverage partnerships with music schools and indie labels to attract new artists and listeners.
Relevant: Align goals with the overarching vision of empowering emerging artists and creating a dedicated community.
Time-bound: Reach the above objectives within a 6-month period post-launch.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Monthly Active Users (MAUs): Target 100,000 MAUs within the first 6 months.
Artist Sign-ups: Aim for 10,000 new artists registering on the platform in the first quarter.
Revenue Growth: Generate $200,000 in subscription-based revenue in the first year.
Qualitative Objectives
Enhance user experience by integrating feedback loops and conducting regular user surveys.
Foster a vibrant community where users frequently engage with artists and their content by providing interactive features like live chats and Q&A sessions.
Strategic Alignment
SoundBubble's objectives align seamlessly with the company's mission of revolutionizing the music industry. By focusing on emerging artists, we aim to create new revenue streams and amplify our brand presence. Synergies with existing projects such as our Artist Development Program will further bolster our market position.

Risk Mitigation
Risks: Potential platform scalability issues, content moderation challenges, and competitive pressures.
Strategies: Invest in robust infrastructure, develop strict content guidelines, and maintain an agile development process to swiftly address challenges.
Contingency Plans: Establish a rapid response team for technical issues, and devise marketing strategies to counteract competitive moves.
Features
Core Features
Artist Dashboard: A comprehensive interface allowing artists to upload tracks, monitor their performance metrics, and interact with fans.
Music Discovery: An intuitive algorithm-based recommendation system introducing users to new artists and tracks based on their listening patterns.
Social Integration: Features such as sharing, following, comments, and live sessions to enhance user engagement and community building.
User Benefits
Artists: Streamlined music uploading, real-time feedback from listeners, and direct monetization options through subscriptions and donations.
Listeners: Curated playlists, personalized recommendations, and opportunities to support favorite artists directly.
Technical Specifications
Backend: A scalable cloud-based server architecture built on AWS to handle high volumes of streaming data.
Database: Use of MySQL for relational data and MongoDB for handling large volumes of metadata.
Frontend: React.js for a dynamic and responsive user interface.
Feature Prioritization
Must Have: Artist dashboard, music discovery, social integration.
Should Have: Live performance streaming, advanced analytics for artists.
Could Have: Virtual reality (VR) concert experiences, AI-based music creation tools.
Won't Have: Offline listening (initial phase).
Future Enhancements
Integration with virtual reality platforms for immersive concert experiences.
Development of AI tools that help artists create and mix music.
Expansion to include podcasts and radio shows to broaden content offerings.
User Experience
User Interface (UI) Design
Design Principles: Simple, intuitive, and artist-centric. Use wireframes to illustrate the layout and flow of key screens like the home page, artist dashboard, and music player.
Visual Style: Modern and clean design with vibrant accents to highlight interactive elements.
User Journey
Onboarding: Easy sign-up process for both artists and listeners with guided tutorials.
Engagement: User paths from discovering new music to interacting with artists and forming playlists.
Usability Testing
Conduct regular A/B tests to evaluate the effectiveness of new features.
Use heatmaps to understand user interactions and optimize the interface.
Accessibility
Follow WCAG guidelines to ensure the platform is accessible to users with disabilities.
Regularly test and update features to maintain compliance and enhance inclusivity.
Feedback Loops
Implement in-app feedback forms to capture user input.
Regularly analyze feedback and release updates to improve user satisfaction continually.
Milestones
Development Phases
Discovery Phase: Conduct market research, finalize feature set – Duration: 1 month.

Background
Problem Statement
In today's digital age, emerging artists struggle to find platforms where they can seamlessly share their music and grow their fanbase without getting lost in the noise of mainstream content. Many talented individuals don't have the resources or opportunities to promote their music effectively. As a result, they end up earning insufficient revenue to sustain their craft while music lovers miss out on discovering fresh talent.

Market Opportunity
The music streaming industry is poised to grow massively, with projections estimating it to exceed $76.91 billion by 2027. However, there's a clear gap in the market for platforms dedicated to unsigned and emerging talents. Mainstream platforms often overshadow these artists, and there's a significant demand among listeners to discover new music. Competitors like Spotify and Apple Music focus primarily on established artists, leaving a niche yet potentially lucrative market segment untapped.

User Personas
Aspiring Artists
Characteristics: Individuals aged 18-35, tech-savvy, passionate about music creation, and seeking platforms for exposure.
Needs: User-friendly interfaces to upload music, tools to promote their tracks, and opportunities for monetization.
Challenges: Limited promotional budgets, lack of visibility, and insufficient revenue streams.
Avid Music Fans
Characteristics: Individuals aged 15-40, diverse musical tastes, constantly on the hunt for new genres and artists.
Needs: Easy discovery of new music, curated playlists, and social features to share and discuss music.
Challenges: Overwhelmed by mainstream content, difficulty in finding unique, new music.
Vision Statement
SoundBubble aims to democratize music distribution by creating an inclusive platform where emerging artists can showcase their talent, connect with fans, and generate sustainable income. By harnessing the power of community-driven discovery and advanced technology, SoundBubble will redefine the landscape of music streaming, making it a haven for both artists and fans.

Product Origin
The idea for SoundBubble emerged from a recognition of the challenges faced by new artists in gaining visibility and achieving financial success. Initial brainstorming sessions with artists and music industry experts highlighted the urgent need for a dedicated platform. Early pilot studies were conducted where a small group of artists uploaded their tracks and engaged with users, providing invaluable feedback that shaped the concept into a scalable product idea.

Objectives
SMART Goals
Specific: Achieve a 25% increase in user base by Q1 through targeted marketing campaigns and platform enhancements.
Measurable: Track user growth, artist sign-ups, and revenue increments via analytics dashboards.
Achievable: Leverage partnerships with music schools and indie labels to attract new artists and listeners.
Relevant: Align goals with the overarching vision of empowering emerging artists and creating a dedicated community.
Time-bound: Reach the above objectives within a 6-month period post-launch.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Monthly Active Users (MAUs): Target 100,000 MAUs within the first 6 months.
Artist Sign-ups: Aim for 10,000 new artists registering on the platform in the first quarter.
Revenue Growth: Generate $200,000 in subscription-based revenue in the first year.
Qualitative Objectives
Enhance user experience by integrating feedback loops and conducting regular user surveys.
Foster a vibrant community where users frequently engage with artists and their content by providing interactive features like live chats and Q&A sessions.

SoundBubble's objectives align seamlessly with the company's mission of revolutionizing the music industry. By focusing on emerging artists, we aim to create new revenue streams and amplify our brand presence. Synergies with existing projects such as our Artist Development Program will further bolster our market position.

Strategies: Invest in robust infrastructure, develop strict content guidelines, and maintain an agile development process to swiftly address challenges.
Contingency Plans: Establish a rapid response team for technical issues, and devise marketing strategies to counteract competitive moves.

Social Integration: Features such as sharing, following, comments, and live sessions to enhance user engagement and community building.

Artists: Streamlined music uploading, real-time feedback from listeners, and direct monetization options through subscriptions and donations.
Listeners: Curated playlists, personalized recommendations, and opportunities to support favorite artists directly.

Database: Use of MySQL for relational data and MongoDB for handling large volumes of metadata.
Frontend: React.js for a dynamic and responsive user interface.

Must Have: Artist dashboard, music discovery, social integration.
Should Have: Live performance streaming, advanced analytics for artists.

Integration with virtual reality platforms for immersive concert experiences.

Expansion to include podcasts and radio shows to broaden content offerings.

prompts.description:
Product Backlog
Example
Product Backlog for Techy Running App
Product Vision
This section sets the direction for your product by clearly defining its ultimate aim. It describes the value the product will deliver to customers and its alignment with the company's strategic goals and broader mission. A compelling vision serves as a guiding star, ensuring the team remains focused and aligned.

Vision Statement
Compose a concise and motivational vision statement.
Focus on customer-centric and outcome-driven results.
Highlight unique differentiators from competitors.
Vision: 'Techy Running aims to revolutionize the running experience by providing a comprehensive, personalized, and community-driven platform that inspires and supports runners of all levels.'

Strategic Alignment
Illustrate alignment between the product vision and overall company strategy.
Emphasize key objectives the product seeks to achieve.
Maintain consistency with the company’s mission and core values.
Strategic Alignment: This app directly supports our company’s mission to foster a healthier lifestyle by leveraging technology. Key objectives include enhancing user engagement through advanced tracking features and building a robust community through social features.

Product Goals
Articulate the primary goals that drive the realization of the product vision. Goals should be SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound) to facilitate clear understanding and effective tracking. These goals are essential in guiding the development process and optimizing prioritization.

Goal Definition
Articulate goals with clarity and precision.
Define measurable endpoints and KPIs.
Ensure goals are realistic given the available resources.
Launch MVP by Q2 2022: The MVP should include basic tracking functionalities like distance, pace, and calories burned, alongside a simple user onboarding process.
Gain 500,000 users by the end of 2022, measured through app installations and active users. Leverage marketing channels and introductory offers to drive user acquisition.
Maintain a 4.5+ rating on the App Store, tracked via user reviews and ratings. Implement regular updates and customer support to address user feedback swiftly.
Relevance and Alignment
Validate goals against broader business objectives.
Align goals with market needs and customer expectations.
Ensure goals contribute to strategic long-term success.
Each of these goals has been selected to ensure the initial delivery and market penetration of the app. They align closely with our mission of promoting a healthier lifestyle.

Time-bound Targets
Set achievable deadlines for each goal.
Establish a timeline to track progress and milestones.
Regularly review deadlines and adjust as necessary.
MVP ready by June 30, 2022.
User acquisition goal measured monthly, with marketing campaigns tailored to meet this target.
Regular monitoring of app reviews to ensure the rating stays above 4.5.
Features/Items
This section offers an overview of the key features of the product, including scope and estimated completion times. Prioritize these features in alignment with product goals and customer demands to ensure stakeholders understand essential functionalities and their significance.

User Interface
Estimated Time: 2 Sprints Priority: High

User Stories
Craft user stories that clearly describe the user, their needs, and rationale.
Ensure stories are succinct and outcome-focused.
Prioritize user stories based on impact and business value.
User Stories:

As a user, I want to register and set up my profile to personalize my experience.
As a user, I want to input my running data manually so I can track my progress.
Acceptance Criteria
Define clear conditions for feature acceptance.
Use tangible, testable criteria linked to user stories.
Ensure all stakeholders agree on the criteria.
Acceptance Criteria:

User can create and edit their profile.
Data fields for manual running data entry are present.
Profile setup confirms based on predefined data validation rules.
Training Plans
Estimated Time: 3 Sprints Priority: Medium

User Stories
As a user, I want to get personalized training plans tailored to my fitness level and goals so that I can improve efficiently.
As a user, I want to adjust my training plan based on my progress so that it remains challenging and achievable.
Acceptance Criteria
Personalization algorithm is working effectively, providing differentiated training plans.
Users can customize their plan settings and goals.
Training plans adjust based on user feedback and performance data.
Backlog Priority
Organize backlog items based on their ROI to ensure the most valuable tasks are addressed first. High-priority items should closely align with strategic objectives and customer needs for optimal resource use.

The 'User Interface' feature is the top priority because it's crucial for user onboarding and vital for MVP. The 'Training Plans' is the second priority and will be the key selling point of our app, but it relies on user data gathered via the UI.

Ranking Criteria
Evaluate ROI for each backlog item.
Incorporate both quantitative and qualitative measures.
Maintain a consistent ranking methodology.
Ranking is based on the immediate impact on user experience and business objectives.

Strategic Impact
Align high-priority items with strategic objectives.
Assess the contribution of each item to overall success.
Adapt prioritization based on market conditions and feedback.
The completion of 'User Interface' aligns directly with our strategic goal of user acquisition. 'Training Plans' will support user retention and satisfaction.

Resource Allocation
Distribute resources according to item priority.
Ensure critical items receive necessary focus.
Manage balance between effort and anticipated outcomes.
Resources have been allocated to ensure the 'User Interface' is completed first, followed by 'Training Plans' once initial user data is available.

prompts.description:
FitFuture Product Roadmap
Product Vision
FitFuture aims to revolutionize the wearable technology space by providing personalized, real-time health and fitness tracking to enable individuals to lead healthier lives.

Problem Statement
Many fitness wearables fall short in providing personalized insights and real-time tracking. According to a recent survey, 65% of wearable users feel their devices offer generic insights that are not actionable. FitFuture addresses this gap by combining artificial intelligence with advanced biometrics to offer personalized health recommendations.

Target Audience
Our primary target audience includes active individuals aged 18-45 who prioritize fitness and are comfortable using technology to track personal health and fitness data. Insights from market research indicate that this demographic values precise, actionable health insights and is willing to invest in premium solutions for their well-being.

Value Proposition
FitFuture stands out by offering a unique blend of real-time data analysis and personalized health recommendations. By integrating AI and biometrics, it provides actionable insights tailored to individual users, surpassing the generic advice offered by many existing wearables. This level of personalization not only enhances user experience but also drives better fitness outcomes.

Vision Summary
To be the leading provider of personalized, real-time fitness, and health tracking solutions.

Motivation & Inspiration
The inspiration for FitFuture stemmed from observing the struggle many people face in making sense of their fitness data. Existing solutions were often too generic and failed to offer actionable insights. Detailed market research and user interviews highlighted the demand for a device that doesn't just track but also interprets data to offer personalized health recommendations.

Product Strategy
To be the leading wearable technology that provides custom, real-time health and fitness insights.

Objective
Our main objective is to increase our market share in the wearable technology space by 15% within the first two years.

Key Results
Sign on 50,000 users by the end of Q1.
Achieve 25% market penetration by Q3.
Attain a customer satisfaction rating of 85% by Q4.
Strategic Initiatives
AI Integration: Develop advanced AI algorithms to provide deeper insights and personalized recommendations. This involves extensive R&D and partnerships with AI experts.
Partnerships: Form strategic partnerships with leading fitness centers and health clinics to promote FitFuture and provide integrated health solutions. Target at least ten major partnerships by Q2.
Community Engagement: Build an online community of users to share experiences, advice, and progress, fostering a supportive environment. Launch an engaging community platform within the first six months.
Success Metrics
User Growth: Track the number of new users acquired monthly with a target growth rate of 10% per month.
Engagement Rates: Measure the frequency of app usage and feature utilization, aiming for an average daily engagement of 60% among active users.
Customer Retention: Monitor the percentage of users who continue using the product over the long term, targeting a retention rate of 75% within the first year.
Net Promoter Score (NPS): Regularly survey users to gauge their likelihood of recommending FitFuture to others, aiming for an NPS score of 50 or above.
Competitive Analysis
FitFuture faces competition from brands like Fitbit and Apple Watch, which have strong brand recognition but often offer generic fitness tracking. Our personalized AI-driven insights differentiate us by providing tailored health recommendations, addressing a clear gap in the market. Additionally, our emphasis on real-time data and actionable insights positions us uniquely against these established players.

Product Roadmap
Timeline
Q1: Product Launch
Q2: Feature Enhancement
Q3: Market Expansion
Q4: Customer Retention
Milestones
Q1: Launch of FitFuture along with an initial marketing blitz across digital platforms.
Q2: Rollout of sleep tracking feature and integration with popular health apps.
Q3: Expansion into European markets, supported by localized marketing campaigns.
Q4: Launch of customer loyalty program and introduction of premium subscription plans.
Feature Prioritization
Features are prioritized based on user impact, development effort, and alignment with strategic goals. High-priority features include real-time health analytics, sleep tracking, and social sharing functionalities. Additionally, user feedback will play a critical role in shaping our product roadmap, ensuring we address the most critical user needs.

Resource Allocation
Development: Allocate 50% of the budget to ensure the development of robust and innovative features that differentiate us in the market.
Marketing: Dedicate 30% of the budget for targeted campaigns, influencer partnerships, and promotional events to build brand awareness.

Monthly Updates: Provide detailed reports on progress, challenges, and next steps to all stakeholders, enhancing transparency and alignment.
Quarterly Meetings: Conduct strategic reviews with key stakeholders to assess performance and realign objectives if necessary.
User Feedback Sessions: Host regular feedback sessions with users to gather insights and guide feature development and improvements.
